To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the threshold condition on proton fraction for direct URCA reactions in neutron stars with large magnetic fields is relaxed, and the initial magnetic fields of neutron stars are constrained.
direct Urca process in neutron stars is allowed for any concentration of protons in the presence of strong magnetic fields.
the direct URCA reactions can be open for any proton concentration if the proton Landau level is filled, and the initial field in pulsars is constrained to be less than 1014 G.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the direct URCA reactions in neutron stars with very strong magnetic fields, in the context of the problem of neutron star cooling.
the direct URCA processes in the core of neutron stars.
the direct URCA processes in strongly magnetized degenerate matter.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, for a neutron star with an initial magnetic field of 10 14 G, the direct URCA reaction is open if the proton concentration is larger than about 0.2, and that the neutron star will cool down rapidly.
direct URCA is open for a wide range of magnetic field strengths and proton concentrations in neutron star cores.
, in the case of the direct URCA processes, the magnetic field can be large enough to suppress the URCA processes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, if the direct URCA reactions occur in neutron stars, the magnetic field should be larger than ~10 14 G.
, the magnetic field inside pulsars is likely to be larger than 10 12 G.
the initial magnetic field of pulsars is not larger than 2 × 10 ^{14} G, and is likely to be much smaller.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, for the same initial proton fraction, the threshold for the direct URCa process is lowered by the magnetic field.
the initial magnetic field strength of a neutron star is limited to be less than ~1014 G, for a typical pulsar age of ~10^6 yrs.
the direct URCA reactions may take place in neutron stars with a strong magnetic field, which has important consequences for the cooling of neutron stars.
